chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a group of thieves who had stolen, so he cut their hands from the middle of the palm and left the thumb, not cutting it off. He ordered them to enter the guest house, ordered that their hands be treated, and fed them ghee, honey, and meat until they recovered.

Then he called for them and said: 'O هؤلاء, your hands have already gone ahead to the Fire. So if you repent, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows the sincerity of your intention, Allah will accept your repentance, and you will draw your hands to Paradise. But if you do not repent and do not desist from what you are upon, your hands will drag you to the Fire.'

key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, the abode of punishment
key_terms.الْكَفِّ: the palm of the hand, specifying the place of amputation in context
key_terms.تُبْتُمْ: you repent; return from sin to obedience
key_terms.دَارَ الضِّيَافَةِ: the guest house, indicating a place of care and lodging

ai.seo_question: How did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام deal with thieves after carrying out the hadd punishment for theft?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام carried out the legal punishment for theft while also ensuring medical treatment and care for those punished. He then exhorted them to sincere tawbah, teaching that repentance can transform a sinful act into a path toward salvation, whereas persistence in sin leads to the Fire.
